problem: A design in design mode never states how the system will be structured at runtime. The design directory carries three diagrams keyed to the narrative levels: a container overview, a sequence flow, and a class inventory of data types. Nothing in the set answers Nexus's question of which services, libraries, data stores, and external systems the design will create and which protocol crosses each boundary. Nothing validates the drafted architecture before the engineer reads it, so the engineer is the only pair of independent eyes on a draft the drafting session wrote. When a design introduces an endpoint surface or an entity model, those contracts exist only in prose inside the ADR or the class diagram, nowhere reviewable as a whole. And nothing creates DDD-VOCABULARY.md: design stage 1 loads it if present, stage 5 updates an existing file, review never reads it, and implement's vocabulary agent reads it in full per slice — so a repo that never made one runs the entire lifecycle against a glossary that does not exist, with the vocabulary agent at risk of a silent CLEAN.
why_now: The comparison against Nexus's pipeline workflow landed this week and showed both systems arriving at the same generate-review-approve shape with different enforcement. Nexus's architecture brief specifies the runtime diagram contract and the pass-cube evaluation gate; the merged options mode (ADR-0035) already accepted inline SVG as the working exception to the shared mermaid pipeline, and a colleague's hand-authored SVG architecture review at think-with-ai showed the shape working end to end; harnesses and models now follow skill instructions well enough that a session-spawned reviewer and a named diagram contract need no new install surface. The RED/GREEN/VALIDATE roles already prove the independent-reviewer pattern works in this family, and the viewer record index gives every new artifact a place to land without new joins.
approach: One named diagram slot, one optional artifact, one stage-6 reviewer, one glossary bootstrap. The runtime architecture diagram lives at docs/architecture/designs/<name>/diagrams/runtime-architecture.svg — authored directly as inline SVG, not mermaid — compiled by build_index.py to record["diagrams"]["runtime"] and rendered by the viewer as the lead tile inside the design's architecture level, ahead of the class diagram, with the level-1 overview untouched as the leading diagram of the design. Its contract is a new architect reference, plugins/architect/skills/architecture/references/runtime-architecture-diagram.md, translating Nexus's hard rules: clustered boundaries for client, api, data, infra, and external; shape semantics (cylinders for data stores, dashed for external systems, rounded for services); every boundary edge labeled with its protocol; 8 to 30 nodes; one page; a viewBox and no external references, checked by a structural validator plugins/architect/scripts/check_design_svg.py in the pattern of check_options_report.py, which ADR-0035 already accepted as the exception to the shared mermaid pipeline. Stage 6 spawns a reviewer before the engineer reads: it validates the draft against a blind rubric derived from goal.json and intent.json, then re-explores alternatives seeded with the final draft, and its findings enter stage 6 as classified challenges the engineer adjudicates; endorsed survivors reach intent.alternatives only through the stage-4 record, which alone fills that field per ADR-0035. contracts.md joins the design directory as an optional artifact carrying the envisioned API endpoints and data models, shown before write, skipped with a stated reason when the design touches no public interface. Every architect and implement mode checks for DDD-VOCABULARY.md; when design stage 1 finds it absent, a vocabulary bootstrap proposes term candidates from the baseline-verified districts and real code symbols, annotates each with its DDD kind from kind-matched corpus/principles/ddd cards, grills the engineer — confirm, rename, reject, and the inverted what-would-you-call-this question — using corpus/scenarios/architecture_ddd/004_ubiquitous_language_naming.yaml as the question bank and 003_bounded_context_splitting.yaml for cross-context scoping, then writes the glossary at the target root or in the bundle dir; options mode checks at stage 1 and offers the bootstrap at hand-off, review reports the absence as a P1 finding and offers at run end, implement's modes surface a notice, and implement:vocabulary never returns a silent CLEAN from a missing file. Reviewer spawns run on glm-5.3-flash:cloud per the engineer's standing directive.

alternatives.option: Reserve diagrams/level-0.mmd and shift the numbered levels so the runtime diagram leads the design
alternatives.rejected_because: The numbered keys are load-bearing everywhere: build_index.py compiles by the level-{1,2,3} filename loop, the viewer's record tiles filter the levels list, and the readiness check fails a level whose key is empty. Renumbering risks every consumer at once, and the engineer asked that the overview keep leading the design.

alternatives.option: Make the runtime diagram the design's fourth narrative level
alternatives.rejected_because: Design mode caps a design at three levels because a design has no diff, only a pull request does. A fourth narrative level also puts the runtime picture beside the file-changes slot the PR contract reserves, and touches more viewer call sites than the design needs.

alternatives.option: Upgrade the per-PR level-1 brief so PR diagrams follow the runtime contract
alternatives.rejected_because: The engineer ruled it out: at PR stage the architecture is already written and the runtime diagram belongs to architecture:design. The per-PR contract stays diff-grounded, three levels.

alternatives.option: Enforce the review as a hard gate, three independent reviews all passing before design mode completes, as Nexus does with pass^3 before execution
alternatives.rejected_because: Nexus's gate evaluates executed work against a PRD; pre-code, our assessment discipline marks every finding kind prediction, and a numeric blocker would dress a prediction as a check. The reviewer enters stage 6 as advisory challenges first; the hard form stays available for implement Gate 2 if the advisory form proves toothless.

alternatives.option: Carry endpoints and data models as new fields inside intent.json
alternatives.rejected_because: intent.json is the interview record, and stage 2 deliberately collects five topics only. Endpoints and data models are drafted artifacts, not interview facts, so they belong in a separate contracts file the engineer shows before write, not in the author's stated intent.

alternatives.option: Keep authoring the runtime diagram in mermaid at the named slot
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-0035 already accepted inline SVG as the exception to the shared mermaid pipeline because mermaid cannot carry the emphasis borders and badges the runtime picture needs, and the engineer preferred SVG after a colleague's hand-authored SVG architecture review showed the shape. Mermaid stays for the three narrative levels, which the shared pipeline compiles and validates.

alternatives.option: Move the stage-6 re-explore into the new options mode
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-0035 scopes options mode to the whole system once, before a design exists, and forbids it running exploration; the reviewer closes the loop after one design's draft exists. Endorsed survivors route through the engineer into stage 4's intent.alternatives, which alone fills that field.

alternatives.option: Have implement modes auto-run the vocabulary bootstrap when the file is missing
alternatives.rejected_because: The glossary is written by consent, from an interview. A build surface that silently interviews the engineer mid-feature violates the check-for-existence rule the engineer set; implement surfaces a notice and points at design, where the bootstrap belongs.

out_of_scope: A DAG execution workflow or any orchestration engine; coding harnesses and models follow skill instructions, and RED/GREEN/VALIDATE already governs execution
The pass^k automated hard gate at design review; the stage-6 reviewer is advisory in this design
Any change to the per-PR diagram contract, its levels, or build_diagrams.py validation
Glossary Non-Goals work; intent.out_of_scope and goal.abort_if already cover them end to end
Ship a new agent file anywhere; the reviewer is session-spawned under the ADR-0005 dual-path pattern, and ADR-0025 keeps implement the only agent-owning plugin
Authoring content for corpus/scenarios/ddd/, which holds only a README today; the bootstrap cites only scenarios/architecture_ddd until real scenario files exist
risks: Hand-authored SVG bypasses the shared mermaid validation, so a broken file renders blank; the structural validator (viewBox, titled groups, no external references) is the mitigation
The stage-6 reviewer adds spawn latency to every design round, and the churn-detection budget now shares room with reviewer retries
A blind rubric written from goal.json alone is thin pre-code, so scores can inflate; the mitigation is mandatory citation and the advisory classification
The vocabulary bootstrap interviews the engineer, so a heavy repo could spawn a long interview; the grill is capped at the terms the districts name
testing: uv run shared/build_index.py over the self bundle with the new design artifacts present; uv run plugins/architect/scripts/check_design_svg.py over this design's runtime-architecture.svg and each fixture; pytest on build_index and viewer tests; manual render of the design route in the View server; a real end-to-end run against the visualisation-decision-memory design in the think-with-ai repo, producing its runtime-architecture.svg
reviewer_focus: The record-index shape: does record["diagrams"]["runtime"] break any of the viewer call sites that filter or read the diagrams dict
The blind rubric derivation: does the reviewer read goal.json and intent.json before the draft, and never the ADR
The contracts skip rule: a design with no public surface must state its skip, not go silent
unknowns: Whether mermaid C4 System_Boundary renders clusters acceptably across the viewer's themes
Whether one reviewer spawn per round is enough, or whether the round budget needs k configurable before E2 ships
